Destination order:
1) Zone rules: if the zone has its own acceptance protocol, the item must pass it first.
2) A container with its own rule that accepts the item ALWAYS wins over one with no rules at all (Global) - regardless of either one's priority.
3) Priority: among equally specific containers (all with their own rule, or all Global), zone priority decides first, then container priority.
4) Affinity: if priority is still tied, the container that already holds that same item (or its family) is preferred.
If no valid destination has space, the item stays in your inventory.

Requires Debug mode ON. Logs when Better Sorting's flat category code is normalized back to the vanilla category (Food/Weapon/Accessory/Material/FirstAid/Gardening) before our own subcategory engine evaluates it. Per-item detail lives in the separate >>> DETAIL sublog.
Requires Debug mode ON. Retroactive recipe grants from manuals already read, and free-crafting overrides. Low volume - useful when a recipe won't show up in the crafting menu.
Requires Debug mode ON. Deposits, bulk redistribution jobs, and item category/subcategory tagging.
Requires Debug mode ON. Logs every time the inventory right-click context menu fires and whether the Storage window is visible at that moment, to diagnose why the Transfer option is not showing up.

Requires Debug mode ON. Logs, per literature row shown in Storage, whether the recipe probe succeeded and what it returned, so the already-read checkmark can be verified against real data instead of guesses.
Requires Debug mode. Summarizes client/server commands, sequence and synchronization state. Full payloads remain in the separate >>> DETAIL block.

Requires Debug mode ON. Applying a container's display name to its in-world object (menu/inventory name). Separate from the "SiK UI:" entries above - this is naming logic, not the UI framework itself.

Requires Debug mode. Bounded traces for character UUID lifecycle, faction/online roster merging, idempotent member changes and identity invariants. Names are diagnostic only and never authorize access.
Requires Debug mode. Summarizes destination selection for deposits and Auto Sort. Per-node decisions remain in the separate >>> DETAIL block.
Requires Debug mode ON. Traces the scroll/virtual-list engine shared by every scrollable panel and the Storage tab's item list: row-pool growth and dataset changes.

Requires Debug mode ON. Traces every change in the Items tab search box: UTF-16 unit length vs real Unicode character length, and the received text. Meant for diagnosing search in non-ASCII languages (Chinese, Japanese, Korean...).

Requires Debug mode ON. Traces resolved column widths for every table built with the shared SiK_UI.Table framework (Storage, Zones and nodes, Network, Permissions...). Only logs when the available width actually changes (e.g. window resize), never every frame.
Requires Debug mode ON. Traces the side tab rail and the Core/add-on tab-registration contract: panel creation/reuse, visibility toggles, and tab click activation/cancellation.

Requires Debug mode ON. Logs every button click and terminal-window lifecycle event (open/reuse/refresh), and dumps the on-screen widget tree with positions and overlaps, to console.txt with prefix [GS_UI]. This is the general/master trace for our own UI framework (SiK UI) - see the other "SiK UI:" entries below for narrower categories (table geometry, scroll, tabs, search).
Requires Debug mode ON. Every proximity/access check against a terminal (manifest, registry, range evaluation). Fires repeatedly while trying to open a terminal - very verbose.
Requires Debug mode ON. The "how much do I have in my network" tooltip patch on vanilla item tooltips (render failures, fallback path used).
Requires Debug mode ON. Logs every zone creation attempt (name, source, network, bounds), whether it exactly matches an already-registered zone, and the current zone count against the sandbox limit.
Requires Debug mode and Capacity bonus. High-volume sublog: one line per live container with a detected personal bonus, on every terminal refresh. Enable only for a targeted capacity diagnosis.
Requires Debug mode and Category compatibility. High-volume sublog: one line per item classified via Better Sorting's normalization table. Enable only for a targeted category-mapping diagnosis.
Requires Debug mode and Crafting. High-volume sublog: records known-recipe probes, individual loan/return decisions and batch internals. Enable only for a targeted crafting diagnosis.

Requires Debug mode and Inventory/transfers. Massive sublog: may print one classification line per item/type, including category, subcategory and leaf. Enable only when diagnosing filters or snapshots.
Requires Debug mode and Network traces. High-volume sublog: records full command/payload flow. A SYSTEM warning appears before DETAIL lines. Enable only for a targeted network diagnosis.
Requires Debug mode and Routing. High-volume sublog: records the evaluated tier and capacity result for every candidate node. Enable only for a targeted deposit/Auto Sort diagnosis.

WARNING: Any enabled debug logging can reduce game and server performance; DETAIL logs may generate massive output. Use only for targeted diagnostics, enable only the required >> blocks, and disable during normal play and on production servers.

Enabled by default. Sends enabled Core/add-on log lines from the dedicated server to subscribed client consoles in bounded batches. Lines keep [SRV]/[CLI] origin markers. Disable it to keep diagnostics only on the server.

When ON, a container joins the network regardless of distance to the nearest active terminal, and a new terminal links to any existing network with no distance limit. Not recommended outside testing: defeats the purpose of a physical terminal. OFF by default: enforces 'Network reach', like in a normal game.

When ON, the network UI can be opened from anywhere, without needing a physical GS terminal nearby or being within tablet wireless range. Useful for testing or creative play. OFF by default: requires a terminal or tablet, like in a normal game.

Requires 'Consume generator fuel' ON (experimental, still being tested). Tries to also include batteries from solar mods (Immersive Solar Arrays, Plysken Solar Revolution) in the consumption split, alongside regular generators. Since this relies on those mods' internal data, it's not guaranteed to keep working if they change their internal format; if it stops detecting them, the network simply won't drain that source, no errors.

EXPERIMENTAL, still being tested. OFF by default out of caution: the network consumes nothing, it just requires power to be present (see 'Require electricity' above, that one is stable). If turned ON, while the network is running off a nearby active generator (never off the normal grid, before the blackout), fuel is slowly drained according to 'Base consumption' and 'Per-container consumption'.

Requires 'Consume generator fuel' ON (experimental, still being tested). Instead of only using the nearest generator, looks for all generators/batteries inside the same building as the terminal and splits consumption across all of them.

OFF by default: the GS Soldering Iron is the one item in this mod meant to be find-only, since it's the tool every other GS recipe needs. Turn ON if you'd rather not depend on a lucky find - the recipe still needs its own magazine read and a real Electricity skill check (see the option below), it just becomes reachable at all.

Requires 'Consume generator fuel' ON (experimental). Fuel the network drains per in-game hour just for being active, before adding per-container consumption. Same unit the generator itself uses (like the vanilla 'Generator fuel consumption' option).
Requires 'Consume generator fuel' ON (experimental). Extra fuel the network drains per in-game hour, multiplied by the number of containers/nodes it has registered. Bigger networks consume more.

Reject deposit if no matching container

If an item has no matching category/filter, exact-item affinity, or canonical taxonomy affinity, keep it in the player's inventory instead of dropping it into the first available 'Any' container. OFF by default (generic containers remain available, as before).
Allows inserting and withdrawing items from the network via the terminal UI without physically walking to the container. Turn OFF for a more realistic experience.

The network only operates when there's power near the controller terminal (normal grid or generator; also checks a radius around it, not just the exact tile). Turn OFF to keep the network always active regardless of electricity.
Players must read GS manual magazines before seeing and crafting each GS item, mirroring how vanilla skill books work. Turn OFF to unlock all GS recipes immediately.
GS recipes can only be crafted at a work surface (table, counter, etc.). Turn OFF to allow hand-crafting anywhere without a surface.
Updates all zone containers every time a player opens the terminal. Recommended ON. Turn OFF only if containers rarely change and you want to reduce server load.
Worn clothing, held weapons and carried bags are never moved by 'Store all'. Recommended ON.
Items marked as favourite in the inventory are skipped by 'Store all'. Recommended ON to protect important items from being accidentally deposited.

Maximum tile distance, measured from the nearest active terminal, within which a container can join the network AND a new terminal can link to an existing one (one single value for both). Only applies when 'Require network reach' is ON. 40 tiles comfortably covers most single houses.
How long installing a network disk on a computer takes (reader + disk method). Shared by the core mod and any addon that installs its own disk on a terminal.
Maximum floor difference from the primary terminal for an additional terminal to count as within coverage. 0 = unlimited (any floor or basement counts as long as it's within the horizontal range).
Maximum horizontal distance from a network's primary terminal within which an additional terminal counts as part of that coverage and can be linked to it on install.
How close a player must stand to a GS terminal furniture to open the network without a tablet (in tiles). Only applies when 'Require terminal' is ON.
1.44 MB of software that survived the apocalypse better than most people did.
Unformatted, unlabeled, and full of potential. Whatever ends up on it is entirely your doing.
One program, one purpose: teaching a terminal to keep its own Floppy Drive plugged in, so it doesn't have to ride in your pockets anymore.
One program, one purpose: politely evicting a SiK terminal from whatever it's plugged into.
Translates buttons and cables into something the computer understands. A quiet little polyglot.
Plenty of keys for typing passwords nobody's ever going to check again.
"GS Disk Utilities": step-by-step instructions for writing a program onto a blank disk. Requires standing close enough to a terminal to bother.
"GS Disk Tools": step-by-step instructions for writing the disk that installs the Floppy Drive into a terminal's network. Requires standing close enough to a terminal to bother.
"GS Disk Tools": step-by-step instructions for writing the disk that carries the GS network's own operating system. Requires standing close enough to a terminal to bother.
"Home Computing Digest": build your own PC from spare parts and a blind faith in twenty-year-old electronics.
A scrappy DIY guide to building your own soldering iron out of scavenged parts. Reading it alone won't get you anywhere - somebody has to actually allow this shortcut first.
"GS Network Monthly": the only magazine still publishing on schedule, even with no one left to deliver it.
Holds every other part of the computer together and never gets a thank you.
A metal box shaped like a box. Everything useful happens inside it.
Picks up the SiK network signal from across the room. From across the county, don't push your luck.
The shell that stops the rest of the parts from quitting after the first drop. Recycled sheet metal, undamaged pride.
The reader's brain. Doesn't know there are zombies outside, and honestly, happier that way.
A well-worn soldering iron, put together by someone who clearly knew what they were doing.
Reads whatever the disk tells it to and nothing else. No questions asked, no judgement about your pre-apocalypse life choices.
